svg.aria-label: The full read path on a real app (ENS). Without Veil, the RPC provider drpc logs your IP and every address, linking all your accounts and joining them across every dapp that uses drpc. With Veil, each account's read is intercepted in the page, routed on its own Tor circuit through a blind KPS gateway to drpc, so the provider sees a different exit per account and no IP. It still sees the addresses queried.
svg.text: The full read path on a real app (ENS)
app.ens.domains reads through drpc, an independent RPC provider that also serves many other dapps.

g.text: Without Veil
app.ens.domains -> fetch(POST, eth_call) -> lb.drpc.live. drpc logs your IP and every address you
read, links all your accounts to one person, and joins that with every other dapp that uses drpc.

svg.text: With Veil: one read, one account, one circuit

g.text: Page issues the read
app.ens.domains calls fetch(POST, eth_call) to its RPC provider, lb.drpc.live.
Dapps read straight from the page, so this never goes through the wallet.
Veil intercepts it in the page
A MAIN-world script at document_start wraps window.fetch and XMLHttpRequest.
Known gap, stated honestly: Web Worker fetch and WebSockets are not caught yet.
Route per account, blind the id
Reads the account from params and eth_call calldata (ignores 0x0), picks that account's isolation key.
Blinds the JSON-RPC id so viem's one global counter cannot stitch the routes back together.
Hand off through the extension
ISOLATED-world relay -> background service worker -> offscreen document.
The offscreen document is what lets an MV3 extension host the worker at all.
anon-rpc worker runs the read
A sandboxed null-origin iframe runs hash-pinned tor-js (Tor in WebAssembly), on-chain specifier 0x700dA3...659e.
It has no access to your keys, DOM or cookies. This is where anon-rpc sits.
Over Tor via a blind KPS gateway
The isolation key maps to a Tor circuit dedicated to this account. The gateway (UDP 12298) relays encrypted
bytes only, never sees your traffic or destination: 3 hops -> a per-account exit node -> lb.drpc.live.
What drpc learns now, and what it still learns
Removed: your IP, and the link between accounts (a different exit each, so they look like strangers, on ENS and
on every other dapp). Still visible: the addresses you query. The reply returns up the same path, id restored.
If a provider blocks Tor (HTTP 403)
Known single-chain RPC: re-route to a Tor-friendly RPC on the same chain (e.g. ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com),
still over Tor, only after a real block. Multichain or unknown gateway: your per-site choice (Ask / Block). Never a silent direct connection.

svg.text: Measured over Tor: ENS 13 of 14 reads. Tor's cost: a one-time cold start of about 20 s, then about 1.5 to 3.4 s per read.
3 accounts map to 3 distinct exits. Veil routes reads only, it never touches your keys and your wallet still signs.
